Question: How many warriors did Toghrul provide Temüjin when his wife was captured?
Answer: 20,000

Context: Seismologists are able to employ the arrival times of seismic waves in reverse, in order to image the interior of the Earth. Early advances in this field revealed the existence of a liquid outer core, within which shear waves were not able to propagate, and of a dense solid inner core. These advances led to the development of a layered model of the Earth, having a crust and lithosphere upon its surface, the mantle below, separated within itself by seismic discontinuities at 410 and 660 kilometres, and the outer core and inner core beneath that. More recently, seismologists have been able to produce detailed images of wave speeds within the Earth, in much the same manner as a physician images a body by means of a CT scan. These images have yielded a far more detailed view of the interior of the Earth, and have replaced the simplified layered model with a considerably more dynamic one.
Question: What types of waves do seismologists use to image the interior of the Earth?
Answer: seismic waves

Context: France assumed control of Algeria in the year 1830; it was not, however, until after 1850 that the nation set about in earnest to reconstruct its global empire, concentrating its efforts chiefly upon North and West Africa, as also South-East Asia, with further conquests in Central and East Africa and the South Pacific. Context: Tesla pursued his ideas of wireless lighting and electricity distribution through high-voltage, high-frequency power experiments conducted in New York and in Colorado Springs; and as early as 1893 he advanced pronouncements upon the possibility of wireless communication by means of his devices. Context: Luther composed the hymn "Ach Gott, vom Himmel sieh darein" ("Oh God, look down from heaven"). "Nun komm, der Heiden Heiland" (Now come, Savior of the gentiles), based upon Veni redemptor gentium, became the principal hymn (Hauptlied) for Advent. He transformed A solus ortus cardine into "Christum wir sollen loben schon" ("We should now praise Christ") and adapted Veni Creator Spiritus to "Komm, Gott Schöpfer, Heiliger Geist" ("Come, Holy Spirit, Lord God"). Two hymns upon the Ten Commandments were composed by him: "Dies sind die heilgen Zehn Gebot" and "Mensch, willst du leben seliglich". His hymn "Gelobet seist du, Jesu Christ" ("Praise be to You, Jesus Christ") became the chief hymn for Christmas. For Pentecost he wrote "Nun bitten wir den Heiligen Geist", and for Easter he adopted "Christ ist erstanden" (Christ is risen), based upon Victimae paschali laudes. "Mit Fried und Freud ich fahr dahin", a paraphrase of Nunc dimittis, was intended for the Feast of the Purification, but it became likewise a funeral hymn. He paraphrased the Te Deum as "Herr Gott, dich loben wir" with a simplified form of the melody; this composition became known as the German Te Deum.
Question: What did Herr Gott, dich loben wir become known as ?
Answer: German Te Deum

Context: The decisions and principles applicable in other criminal investigations and arrests apply likewise in cases of civil disobedience. For instance, the suspect must decide whether to grant a consent search of his property, and whether to speak with police officers. It is generally agreed among jurists, and often held by activists, that a suspect's communication with criminal investigators serves no useful purpose and may prove detrimental. Nevertheless, certain civil disobedients have found it difficult to resist responding to the investigators' questions, sometimes from a lack of understanding of the legal ramifications, or from a fear of appearing rude. Moreover, some civil disobedients endeavour to use the arrest as an occasion to make an impression upon the officers. As Thoreau remarked, "My civil neighbor, the tax-gatherer, is the very man I have to deal with--for it is, after all, with men and not with parchment that I quarrel--and he has voluntarily chosen to be an agent of the government. How shall he ever know well that he is and does as an officer of the government, or as a man, until he is obliged to consider whether he will treat me, his neighbor, for whom he has respect, as a neighbor and well-disposed man, or as a maniac and disturber of the peace, and see if he can get over this obstruction to his neighborliness without a ruder and more impetuous thought or speech corresponding with his action."
Question: What reasons cause failure of the disobedience with authorities?
Answer: lack of understanding of the legal ramifications,

Context: The method here described is the most commonly employed form of construction procurement, and is long established and widely recognized. Direct contractual relations subsist between the architect's client and the main contractor. Every subcontractor maintains a direct contractual relation with the main contractor. Question: Whose role is to design the works, prepare the specifications and produce construction drawings, administer the contract, tender the works, and manage the works from inception to completion

Context: Warsaw is situated in east-central Poland, about 300 km (190 mi) distant from the Carpathian Mountains and approximately 260 km (160 mi) from the Baltic Sea; it lies 523 km (325 mi) to the east of Berlin, Germany. Context: Modern Mongolian historians assert that, towards the close of his life, Genghis Khan endeavoured to establish a civil state under the Great Yassa, which would have instituted the legal equality of all individuals, including women. Context: Where a great many workers are willing to labour for extended periods (high supply) and compete for a position that few employers require (low demand), the wage will be low. This is so because competition between workers drives the wage downward. Dish-washing and customer service furnish examples of such employment. Competition amongst workers tends to drive down wages, owing to the expendable nature of the worker in relation to his or her particular post. Where there are few able or willing workers (low supply), yet a considerable demand for the positions (high demand), the wage will be high. This comes about because competition among employers for employees drives the wage upward. Such employment would include positions requiring highly developed skills, rare abilities, or a high level of risk. Competition amongst employers tends to drive up wages, owing to the nature of the employment, since there is a relative shortage of workers for the particular position. Professional and labor organizations may limit the supply of workers, which results in higher demand and greater incomes for their members. Members may also obtain higher wages through collective bargaining, political influence, or corruption.
Question: When there are many workers competing for a few jobs its considered as what?
Answer: low demand

Context: Ctenophores, which range in size from approximately 1 millimeter (0.039 in) to 1.5 meters (4.9 ft), constitute the largest non-colonial animals employing cilia ("hairs") as their primary mode of locomotion. The majority of species possess eight strips, termed comb rows, which extend the entire length of their bodies and bear comb-like bands of cilia, termed "ctenes," arranged in series upon the comb rows; when the cilia are set in motion, those of each comb come into contact with the comb immediately below. The designation "ctenophora" signifies "comb-bearing", deriving from the Greek κτείς (stem-form κτεν-), which denotes "comb", and the Greek suffix -φορος, which signifies "carrying".
Question: What does ctenophore mean in Greek?

Context: The division process commences when the proteins FtsZ1 and FtsZ2 assemble into filaments, and, with the assistance of a protein named ARC6, form a structure termed a Z-ring within the chloroplast stroma. Context: Since 7500 yr ago, the tides and currents have presented a situation very similar to that of the present. Context: In man, this response is set in motion by the binding of complement to antibodies already attached to these microbes, or by the direct attachment of complement proteins to carbohydrate substances upon the surfaces of microbes. Context: Some years prior to his decease, Genghis Khan requested that he be buried without markings, in accordance with the customs of his tribe. Context: In the year 1894, Mr. Tesla commenced an investigation into that which he designated as radiant energy of an "invisible" nature, after he had noticed damaged film in his laboratory in previous experiments (subsequently identified as "Roentgen rays" or "X-Rays"). Soon thereafter, a great portion of Tesla's early research-comprising hundreds of invention models, plans, notes, laboratory data, tools, and photographs, valued at $50,000-was lost in the fire which consumed his laboratory on 5th Avenue in March of 1895. Context: The words "Bairn" and "hyem", signifying "child" and "home" respectively, exemplify Geordie terms derived from Scandinavian languages; barn and hjem are the corresponding modern Norwegian and Danish forms. Certain words of the Geordie dialect are employed elsewhere in the Northern United Kingdom. The words "bonny" (meaning "pretty"), "howay" ("come on"), "stot" ("bounce"), and "hadaway" ("go away" or "you're kidding") appear to be used in Scots; "aye" ("yes") and "nowt" (IPA://naʊt/, rhymes with out, "nothing") are found elsewhere in Northern England. Context: Luther's Small Catechism was found to be of great utility in enabling parents to teach their children; in like manner, the Larger Catechism proved effective for pastors. Employing the German vernacular, they set forth the Apostles' Creed in language that was simpler, more personal, and Trinitarian in character. He revised each article of the Creed so as to express the nature of the Father, the Son, or the Holy Spirit. The purpose of Luther was to allow the catechumens to regard themselves as a personal object of the work of the three persons of the Trinity, each of which operates in the catechumen's life. That is to say, Luther depicted the Trinity not as a doctrine for learning, but as persons to be known. The Father creates, the Son redeems, and the Spirit sanctifies, a divine unity with separate personalities. Salvation originates with the Father and draws the believer to the Father. Context: In Europe, the North American theatre of the Seven Years' War is not ordinarily assigned a separate name; the entire international conflict is known as the Seven Years' War. Context: The Yuan dynasty marked the first occasion upon which non-native Chinese people exercised rule over all of China. Within the historiography of Mongolia, it is generally regarded as the continuation of the Mongol Empire. The Mongols are widely known to worship the Eternal Heaven, and, according to traditional Mongolian ideology, the Yuan is considered to be "the beginning of an infinite number of beings, the foundation of peace and happiness, state power, the dream of many peoples, besides it there is nothing great or precious." In the traditional historiography of China, on the other hand, the Yuan dynasty is usually considered the legitimate dynasty falling between the Song dynasty and the Ming dynasty. It should be noted, however, that the Yuan dynasty is traditionally often extended to cover the period of the Mongol Empire prior to Kublai Khan's formal establishment of the Yuan in 1271; this is partly because Kublai had his grandfather Genghis Khan placed on the official record as the dynasty's founder, or Taizu (Chinese: 太祖). Despite the traditional historiography as well as official views, including those of the Ming dynasty which overthrew the Yuan, there also exist Chinese people[who?] who do not consider the Yuan dynasty a legitimate dynasty of China, but rather view it as a period of foreign domination. These latter hold that Han Chinese were treated as second-class citizens[citation needed] and that China stagnated both economically and scientifically.
Question: Some Chinese considered the Yuan a legitimate dynasty, but what did other Chinese think it was?
Answer: a period of foreign domination

Context: Mean monthly temperatures range from around 53 F in January to 82 F in July. High temperatures average 64 to 92 °F (18 to 33 °C) throughout the year. Context: Some modern scholars, such as Fielding H. Garrison, are of the opinion that the origin of the science of geology may be traced to Persia after the Muslim conquests had come to an end. Abu al-Rayhan al-Biruni (973–1048 CE) was among the earliest Persian geologists, whose works included the first writings on the geology of India, hypothesizing that the Indian subcontinent had once been a sea. Drawing upon Greek and Indian scientific literature that had not been destroyed by the Muslim conquests, the Persian scholar Ibn Sina (Avicenna, 981–1037) proposed detailed explanations for the formation of mountains, the origin of earthquakes, and other subjects central to modern geology, thereby providing an essential foundation for the later development of the science. In China, the polymath Shen Kuo (1031–1095) formulated a hypothesis for the process of land formation: based upon his observation of fossil animal shells in a geological stratum in a mountain hundreds of miles from the ocean, he inferred that the land was formed by erosion of the mountains and by deposition of silt.
Question: This person proposed explanations for the origins of earthquakes and the formation of mountains, what was his name?

Context: The Rhine, upon emerging from Lake Constance, pursues a course generally westward as the Hochrhein; it passes the Rhine Falls and is joined by its principal tributary, the river Aare. Context: Justifying Grace or Accepting Grace is that grace which is offered by God to all people, and which we receive through faith and trust in Christ, whereby God pardons the believer's sin. Context: The customary measure of a steam engine's efficiency was denoted by its "duty". The notion of duty was first propounded by Watt to demonstrate the superior efficiency of his engines compared to those of the earlier Newcomen design. Duty denotes the number of foot-pounds of work achieved through the combustion of one bushel, weighing 94 pounds, of coal. The finest specimens of the Newcomen design exhibited a duty of approximately 7 million, whereas the majority yielded but 5 million. Watt's initial low-pressure engines were capable of attaining a duty as great as 25 million, though their average stood at 17. This represented a threefold improvement upon the average Newcomen design. Subsequent Watt engines, furnished with high-pressure steam, augmented this figure to 65 million.
Question: What was the ideal duty of a Newcomen engine?

Context: Following the Greeks, little progress was made in the study of prime numbers until the advent of the 17th century. In 1640 Pierre de Fermat stated, without proof, what is now called Fermat's little theorem, a result later proved by Leibniz and Euler. Fermat also conjectured that all numbers of the form 22n + 1 are prime, these being termed Fermat numbers, and he verified this property up to n = 4 (or 216 + 1). The very next number of this type, however, is composite; 232 + 1 has the prime factor 641, as Euler later demonstrated, and in fact no further Fermat primes have been discovered. The French monk Marin Mersenne examined primes of the form 2p − 1, with p a prime; these are known as Mersenne primes in his honour.
Question: Of what form do Mersenne primes take?
Answer: 2p − 1

Context: From their original homelands in Scandinavia and northern Europe, the Germanic tribes extended their dominion throughout the northern and western regions during the middle period of classical antiquity; in late antiquity, they advanced into southern Europe, subduing the Celts and other peoples; and by 800 CE, they had formed the Holy Roman Empire, the first Germanic empire. It must be observed, however, that there was no genuine systemic continuity from the Western Roman Empire to its Germanic successor, which was famously described as "not holy, not Roman, and not an empire", since a vast multitude of small states and principalities existed in the loosely autonomous confederation. Although by 1000 CE the Germanic conquest of central, western, and southern Europe, west of and including Italy, was complete, excluding only Muslim Iberia, there was, nonetheless, little cultural integration or national identity, and "Germany" remained largely a conceptual term referring to an amorphous area of central Europe.
Question: What was the only region in Europe not conquered by the Germanic tribes?
Answer: Muslim Iberia

Context: Following the death of Tugh Temür in 1332 and the subsequent death of Rinchinbal (Emperor Ningzong) in that same year, the 13-year-old Toghun Temür (Emperor Huizong), the last of the nine successors of Kublai Khan, was summoned back from Guangxi and succeeded to the throne. After the decease of El Temür, Bayan became as powerful an official as El Temür had been at the beginning of his long reign. As Toghun Temür grew, he came to disapprove of Bayan's autocratic rule. In 1340 he allied himself with Toqto'a, Bayan's nephew, who was in discord with Bayan, and banished Bayan by a coup. With the dismissal of Bayan, Toghtogha seized the power of the court. His first administration clearly exhibited fresh new spirit. He also gave a few early signs of a new and positive direction in central government. One of his successful projects was to finish the long-stalled official histories of the Liao, Jin, and Song dynasties, which were eventually completed in 1345. Context: The project must conform to zoning and building code requirements. The construction of a project that fails to adhere to such codes confers no benefit upon the owner. Other legal requirements stem from malum prohibitum considerations, which relate to matters of custom or expectation; for example, the segregation of businesses to a business district and residences to a residential district. An attorney may petition for changes or exemptions in the law governing the land upon which the building is to be constructed, either by contending that a rule is inapplicable-as in the case where the bridge design will not cause a collapse-or that the custom is no longer requisite, since acceptance of live-work spaces has grown within the community.

Context: The Rhine, known in Romansh as Rein, in German as Rhein, in French as le Rhin, and in Dutch as Rijn, is a European river. The most considerable city upon its banks is Cologne, in Germany, where the population exceeds 1,050,000 persons. Context: Materials of great combustibility that leave scant residue, such as wood or coal, were believed to be composed largely of phlogiston; in contrast, non-combustible substances which corrode, like iron, contained but a small quantity. Air was not accounted for in the theory of phlogiston, nor were any preliminary quantitative experiments undertaken to examine the notion; on the contrary, the theory rested upon observations of combustion, in that ordinary objects appeared to grow lighter and to forfeit some substance in the process. The circumstance that a substance such as wood gains in weight upon burning was concealed by the buoyancy of the gaseous products of combustion.
